comments: Transfer-learning experiment: identical architecture to kuralsnet_npu_seg_8x64.json (bottleneck_ch=64, full /8 encoder, shape-identical to the native-resolution checkpoint since this model has no resolution-dependent parameters), but initialized from the native-resolution checkpoint's weights (kurals_logs/.../kuralsnet_npu_seg_e300_..._2026-08-05-21:17:46/results/val_doppler_model.pt, val dice 0.5144) via train.py --finetune, instead of random init, then continued training on the 8x64 dataset. Tests whether the native model's learned low-level feature detectors (conv kernels are resolution-agnostic; only BatchNorm running stats and the QAT EMA observers are calibrated to native-resolution activation statistics and will re-adapt during training) give a better starting point than training from scratch, given all three from-scratch attempts (baseline 0.3070, wide128 0.3049, shallow_encoder 0.2887 val dice) independently plateaued in the same 0.29-0.31 band.
